michelle: hey team :wave: i'm michelle, started today. trying to finish my dev bootstrap on WSL2 (win11) and ran into a few issues — asdf/python/poetry interplay and ssh-agent weirdness. quick TL;DR: asdf shows python 3.11, poetry keeps creating venvs in user cache, and git prompts me for passphrase every time. who should I bug?
raj: welcome michelle :tada: for asdf+poetry we usually manage python with asdf and then tell poetry to create in-project venvs: `poetry config virtualenvs.in-project true`. also make sure asdf shims are on your PATH.
michelle: I ran `poetry config virtualenvs.in-project true` but poetry still used `~/.cache/pypoetry/virtualenvs/...` when I ran `poetry install` in the repo. i'm on Ubuntu in WSL.
olga: are your asdf shims active? run `asdf reshim python` and check `echo $PATH` contains `~/.asdf/shims`. on WSL you might need to export PATH in `~/.bashrc` (or `~/.profile` depending on your shell). also `which python` and `python -V` are helpful.
michelle: `which python` -> `/home/michelle/.asdf/shims/python`, `python -V` -> `3.11.6`. but `poetry env info` shows it's using `/usr/bin/python3` when creating the env.
raj: try explicitly telling poetry which python to use: `poetry env use /home/michelle/.asdf/installs/python/3.11.6/bin/python`. that usually fixes cases where poetry picks the distro python.
michelle: will try. another issue: ssh keys. i added my key to the Windows ssh-agent and `ssh-add -l` in powershell shows it. from WSL `ssh -T git@github.com` still asks for passphrase each time. i saw mention of ssh-agent forwarding but haven't set it up.
ben: on WSL the Windows agent isn't exposed by default. there are a couple of common approaches: use `wsl-ssh-pageant`, `npiperelay`, or run an ssh agent inside WSL and add the key there. i prefer `wsl-ssh-pageant` since it forwards the Windows agent so your Windows credential manager works.
olga: yup — link: https://github.com/benpye/wsl-ssh-pageant. install the Windows side and a tiny helper in WSL. then set `export SSH_AUTH_SOCK=/tmp/ssh_auth_sock` (or whatever the helper advises). avoid copying private keys into WSL.
michelle: awesome, i'll try wsl-ssh-pageant. last question on secrets/envs: where should I store a local REDWOOD_API_KEY for dev? put it in `~/.profile`, repo `.env`, or use direnv? i'm on a shared laptop so want to be careful.
raj: prefer direnv + a user-only store. put secrets in `~/.config/redwood/.env` or a key manager, and load them per-project with `.envrc`. definitely do not commit to git.
michelle: who do I ping for VPN/registry access? i need access to the private model registry and redwood-dev network.
olga: ping `@infra-access` (ben) and file a ticket in `#help` if infra blocks you. ben normally handles VPN & registry perms.
ben: @michelle i added you to the `redwood-dev` VPN group earlier today — you should be able to hit the registry now. let me know if you see a 403.
devops-bot: Account change: michelle added to VPN group redwood-dev by ben at 2024-10-03T10:12:00Z
michelle: quick status update: `poetry env use /home/michelle/.asdf/installs/python/3.11.6/bin/python` worked, poetry now creates `.venv` in the project. installed `wsl-ssh-pageant` and ssh forwarding now works (no passphrase prompts). i'll finish cleaning up dotfiles and add direnv. huge thanks everyone :heart:
